headline: Ether has been pushed down very hard and is sitting just above its $2,028 floor, so a rubber-band bounce back toward $2,100 is likely.

messages.text: Hi all! The idea: buy Ether (ETH) at about $2,060-$2,070 and sell a bit higher later today, around $2,096 to $2,113.

Ether has been squeezed down about 10.6% over the last stretch of hourly candles, like a rubber band stretched very far. Its 1-hour RSI, a 0-100 score of how hard price was pushed, is 26. Under 30 means sellers are very tired.
There is a floor nearby. The lowest price today was $2,028, and a news site (AMBCrypto) is watching the $2,000 level as support, meaning a spot where buyers have often stepped in.
The trading volume on the last hour was almost 7 times the normal amount. Big volume at the bottom often means panic selling, and panic usually runs out of steam.

Many people are scared right now (Fear & Greed score 32, 'Fear'). Bets that the price rises cost almost nothing extra (funding rate 0.0026%), so the crowd is not over-excited. That leaves room for a bounce.
My plan risks little: buy near $2,060, get out at $2,022 if I am wrong, and take profit at $2,096, then $2,113 and maybe $2,142.

argument:
ETH trades at 2,069 (24h -2.6%), after a sharp liquidation-driven flush that took the 24h low to 2,028.32. The case is a mean-reversion bounce from deeply oversold conditions, not a trend-following long. Momentum is stretched: 1h RSI 26.6, 15m RSI 28.5 and 5m RSI 34.4, and the 15m price sits below its lower Bollinger band (2,075.04). Price is 1.5% below the 1h EMA21 (2,113.46) and about 2.9% below the 1h SMA50 (2,142.42), so snap-back targets are close and well defined.

The 1h candle printed 6.93x average volume, consistent with capitulation/forced liquidations (AMBCrypto headline cites a $432M liquidation shock; I only saw the headline). Long liquidations clear leveraged weak hands, and perpetual funding is only +0.0026%, so positioning is not crowded. Fear & Greed is 32 (up from 29), a mild improvement from the prior reading.

Admitted weakness: every moving-average check on all three timeframes is bearish and MACD histograms are negative, and the order-book bid/ask ratio is 0.69. That is why this is a short, tightly-stopped intraday scalp aimed at VWAP (2,096.29) and the 1h EMA21, not a swing hold. The stop sits just under the 2,028.32 low, so the trade is invalidated if the floor breaks. Web research was thin: my searches returned mostly undated or older articles, so I rely mainly on the live snapshot and cite news only as headline-level context.

evidence.plain: Price has been pushed down very hard; sellers may be running out of energy.
Ether fell about a tenth in a short time, like a stretched rubber band.
Today's lowest price is the nearby floor; price is only about 2% above it.
A burst of selling that looks like panic, which tends to burn out.
People are scared, which often happens near short-term lows; the score ticked up slightly.
Almost nobody is paying extra to bet on a rise, so the bullish crowd is not overloaded.

evidence.claim: AMBCrypto headline: 'Will ETH's $432M liquidation shock put $2K support at risk?'
evidence.plain: A big wave of forced selling just happened and $2,000 is the watched floor. (snippet only, headline seen, article not opened)
These are the average prices where price often gets pulled back to after a drop.

plan.risk_reward: about 1:1.4 to the 2,113 target and 1:2.2 to 2,142 (from 2,060 entry)

plan_plain: Buy around $2,060. If it drops to $2,022 (just under today's low), sell to limit the loss, about $38 per ETH. Take profit at $2,096, then $2,113, and maybe $2,142. You could win about $1.40 to $2.20 for every $1 you risk.
